title: Portskill
description: Local port allocation, service control, and truthful listener status.
provenance: Authored 2026-09-23 from the working tree at base commit 714b4e2, including uncommitted Stop verification changes. Responsibilities group code within cli.py; they are not separate deployed services. Focused on core lifecycle and access paths, not an exhaustive feature inventory. Evidence paths are repository-relative; current means source-supported, not a live runtime assertion.

boundaries.title: Current user authority
boundaries.description: CLI operations, project hooks, and managed commands execute with the user's permissions. This is not sandbox isolation.

boundaries.title: Optional HTTP passkey gate
boundaries.description: HTTP UI/API/MCP can use the optional gate. Stdio MCP and direct CLI do not traverse it.

boundaries.title: Observation does not grant ownership
boundaries.description: Other listeners can occupy reserved or released ranges. No implicit permission to terminate them.

scenes.title: One local service registry
scenes.description: Developers and agents share allocation state and service controls.

scenes.title: UI, MCP, and CLI converge
scenes.description: HTTP actions and MCP tools converge on shared operations; dashboard status also reads local observations.

scenes.title: Allocation, observation, and control
scenes.description: Verify shutdown before changing allocation; TCP reachability alone does not establish process ownership.

scenes.title: What Portskill can stop
scenes.description: Tracked processes and configured hooks carry control authority. Other listeners are observed only.
